text: So let's just proceed for two minutes. Sorry, 10:45, it's dinner time. Let's now just mention some definitions and introduce some notation that will be useful to have this general understanding of wireless communication networks. So as I said, let's start from the bottom. Whenever we consider the receiver, the receiver that gets the signal gets the signal plus possibly interference. For now, just consider that there are no other sources of signal. Okay, we have only our intended transmitter. So we have the useful signal coming from the intended transmitter. Other receiver, however, as mentioned, we have noise caused by electronics, different types of noise that is typically modeled as Gaussian noise, right? N zero is used to denote the noise power density at the receiver. So let's be traditional notation to denote the power density of the noise. So how much noise essentially we have at a receiver. When we look instead at the transmitted signal, the signal will be transmitted at a certain power level. So there are stations, for example, that transmit at 48 dB of power. This is quite high or lower power PT.
